sections.h2: Where is Groveland, and why does its location matter when you sell a house here?
sections.html:
Groveland sits in the southwestern part of Lake County, at the crossroads of State Road 50, State Road 19 and State Road 33. The city says it is 27 miles west of downtown Orlando, 35 miles from Walt Disney World and 70 miles from Tampa, so buyers who commute toward Orlando or Clermont are a large part of the audience for a Groveland house.

The city's own history page counts more than 26,800 residents and says many new arrivals came from the Orlando area. That inflow is the reason sellers hear from builders, investors and families at the same time. A Groveland owner can usually weigh several kinds of buyer before choosing how to sell.

sections.h2: What is Groveland's history, and how did it grow into a commuter city?
sections.html:
Groveland began as Taylorville. Two brothers settled the area around 1895 with African American workers to harvest turpentine, built a still north of Lake David, and the settlement took the Groveland name after a city council meeting in 1922. The city celebrated its 100th birthday in 2022.

The local economy moved through perfume, lumber, citrus and tourism, according to the city. Lake County holds more than five hundred lakes, and many of them are in the southern part of the county near Groveland. The same page lists nearby anchors: South Lake Hospital, the National Training Center and the Special Olympics Florida training facility, all within about nine miles.

  • Roads: State Roads 50, 19 and 33 meet in town, with the Florida Turnpike a few minutes away.
  • Education: Lake-Sumter Community College is listed at 11 miles, with extended campuses of the University of Central Florida and Saint Leo University.
  • Local identity: the city markets itself as the City with Natural Charm and keeps a Groveland Historical Society.

sections.h2: What do you need to know about Groveland building permits before selling?
sections.html:
The City of Groveland Building Division handles residential and commercial permits and checks plans against the Florida Building Code. If you did work on the house, such as a roof, windows, an addition or a shed, ask the division whether each job has a closed permit before a buyer's inspector asks.

The division also issues Certificates of Occupancy for new homes, registers building contractors, and keeps the permit and inspection records. Its office is at 6825 SR 50, second floor, and it answers at 352-429-2141, option 2, or by email at permitting@groveland-fl.gov. Posted hours are Monday through Thursday 8 am to 5 pm, and Friday 8 am to 3 pm with remote help from 3 pm to 5 pm. Inspections are scheduled through the city's eTrakit portal, and fire inspections go through the Fire Inspector at 352-467-0493.

  • Pull the permit history for your address before you list or accept an offer.
  • Ask the division how to close out an old permit that never received a final inspection.
  • Keep contractor invoices with the permit numbers in one folder for the buyer.

sections.h2: When do Lake County property taxes come due for a Groveland owner?
sections.html:
The Lake County Tax Collector starts collecting each year on November 1 for the January to December tax year, and the bill goes to the owner's address on the tax roll. If a mortgage company pays through escrow, an escrow code prints on the notice, and the owner still receives a copy.

Taxes turn delinquent on April 1, and the tax collector's page says 3% statutory interest is added then. Payments mailed to the office are judged by postmark. Changes to the name, mailing address or assessed value on the roll go through the Lake County Property Appraiser at 352-253-2150, not the tax collector.

sections.h2: Which exemptions apply to a Groveland home, and what changes at a sale?
sections.html:
Lake County's appraiser page lists a homestead exemption that lowers assessed value by up to $51,411, filed by March 1 for owners who lived in the home on January 1. Approval letters are not mailed, and an approved exemption renews on its own each year unless the use of the property changes.

  • Widow or widower: $5,000 off assessed value, ended by remarriage.
  • Disability: $5,000 with a physician statement on Form DR-416 or a Social Security letter.
  • Limited income senior: up to $50,000 for owners 65 or older, with a household income cap of $38,686 as printed by the appraiser. Lake County and Minneola authorize the full amount, and Clermont, Lady Lake, Mount Dora and Tavares authorize up to $25,000. Groveland is not on that list, so ask the appraiser what applies to your parcel.
  • Veterans and deployed service members: separate exemptions, each with a March 1 deadline.

A sale resets the Save Our Homes cap, so the next owner's first assessment follows just value. Renting out the house or moving away ends a homestead.

sections.h2: Which transfer charges land on a Groveland closing statement?
sections.html: The deed carries Florida documentary stamp tax under section 201.02, and the Lake County clerk collects it with the recording charges when the deed is filed. Ask the clerk or your closing agent for the total on your own deed, because page counts and names change the bill.

sections.h2: What proof can a Groveland owner hand to a buyer's lender or mortgage servicer?
sections.html:
Lake County's appraiser does not write letters confirming a homestead. All exemption data is public, and the appraiser tells owners to print or save the property record card, where green checkmarks mark each granted exemption, and send that to the servicer. The card also shows a working tax estimate, though the official figure is the proposed-tax notice mailed in mid-August.

  • Trust ownership: the applicant needs equitable title or a beneficial interest, and the appraiser can ask for the trust agreement.
  • Contract for deed: eligible only if the contract is recorded with the Clerk of the Court and a copy reaches the appraiser. An ordinary purchase contract does not count.
  • A move within Lake County: homestead does not transfer by itself, so a new application is needed for the new address.

Taxes on a house that is already delinquent are a different matter. Once a certificate is sold, the holder can apply for a deed after two years, so clear any unpaid year before closing.

sections.h2: What are the main ways to sell a Groveland house?
sections.html:
• An agent listing brings showings, a buyer inspection and a repair negotiation.
  • A sale by owner puts contracts, disclosures and recording on you.
  • A cash purchase is priced for the property in its present state, with a closing date set by agreement.

Ask every buyer for written terms, the exact amount you would receive and the date it arrives. Lining up the permit history, the tax bill and any tenant details first makes those offers easier to compare.

faqs.q: Does Groveland have its own building department?
faqs.a: Yes, a Building Division inside city government, reachable at 352-429-2141, option 2.

faqs.q: When are Lake County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Collection starts November 1. The best discount is 4% through November 30, and the gross amount is due by March 31.

faqs.q: Is there a Groveland homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Yes. The Lake County Property Appraiser lists up to $51,411 off assessed value for a permanent residence, with applications due March 1. Approved exemptions renew themselves.

faqs.q: Do I pay documentary stamp tax when I sell in Groveland?
faqs.a: Yes, the deed carries a state tax under section 201.02, collected by the clerk when the deed is recorded. Your closing agent normally settles it.

faqs.q: What if my Groveland house needs repairs before a sale?
faqs.a: You can sell without fixing it, and some buyers purchase as-is. Open permits are different, so ask the Building Division about them first.
